title: Download the Required Software
summary: Checklist of the tools used for the front-end part of the course: the VS Code editor, three VS Code extensions (Live Preview, Prettier, vscode-icons) and the Google Chrome browser for its developer tools.

concepts.heading: Code editor: Visual Studio Code
points: VS Code is Microsoft's free editor and is where all course code is written. Download from code.visualstudio.com.
Some older videos show the Atom editor. Atom has been retired by GitHub, so wherever a video says to open Atom or do something in Atom, do the same thing in VS Code instead.

concepts.heading: VS Code extensions to install
points: Extensions are add-ons that give VS Code extra features. Each link in the article opens the Visual Studio Marketplace page; clicking Install there hands off to the VS Code app.

Live Preview (Microsoft, marketplace id ms-vscode.live-server): shows an HTML file in a browser pane inside VS Code and refreshes as you save. Used from the next section onward to view exercise files (right-click index.html → Show Preview).
Prettier (esbenp.prettier-vscode): an automatic code formatter that fixes indentation and spacing so files stay tidy and readable.
vscode-icons (vscode-icons-team.vscode-icons): replaces the generic file icons in the Explorer sidebar with per-file-type icons, which makes .html, .css and .js files easier to tell apart.
(Extra) You can also install from inside VS Code: open the Extensions view (Cmd+Shift+X on Mac, Ctrl+Shift+X on Windows/Linux), search the name, check the publisher, click Install.
(Extra) To have Prettier run every time you save, enable Settings → 'Format On Save' and set 'Default Formatter' to Prettier. This is why files can re-indent themselves on save in later lessons.

concepts.heading: Browser: Google Chrome
points: Chrome is free and is the browser used throughout the course, mainly for Chrome DevTools, which later lessons rely on heavily (inspecting HTML/CSS, the JavaScript console, etc.).
Install it even if you normally browse with something else, so your screen matches the videos.
(Extra) DevTools opens with F12, Cmd+Option+I (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+I (Windows/Linux), or right-click → Inspect.

task.name: Set up the development environment
task.starting_point: A computer without the course tools installed.
task.goal: Have VS Code with the three extensions, plus Chrome, ready before the HTML section begins.
steps: Download and install VS Code from code.visualstudio.com.
Install the Live Preview extension (publisher Microsoft).
Install the Prettier code formatter extension.
(Extra) Check it works: open any folder in VS Code, create index.html, right-click it and confirm 'Show Preview' appears.
task.expected_result: VS Code opens, the Explorer shows file-type icons, a right-click on an HTML file offers Show Preview, and Chrome is installed with DevTools available.

pitfalls: Following old videos that mention Atom; use VS Code for everything.
Installing a different 'Live Server' style extension instead of Microsoft's Live Preview, then not finding the Show Preview option used in later lessons.
Skipping Chrome and then finding DevTools steps look different in another browser.

playground.coverage: The playground runs code in the browser, so no local install is needed and the lesson does not mention the course toolchain.
gaps_and_ideas: Add a short 'Your toolkit' note to the s01 lesson: what VS Code, Live Preview, Prettier, vscode-icons and Chrome DevTools each do, and that the playground's built-in preview plays the role of Live Preview.
Add a tip box listing the DevTools keyboard shortcuts so learners can inspect the playground's preview iframe.
Optional mini-demo: a 'messy vs Prettier-formatted' toggle showing the same HTML before and after auto-formatting, to explain why indentation changes on save.
